request:
I run a small provisions shop in Madina and I want to keep my price list on the computer instead of in my notebook. I want to add the things I sell with their prices. I want to see everything I sell, and look up the price of one thing. Sometimes I stop selling something, so I want to take it off the list.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: When the price of something goes up or down, do you want to change it on the list? If so, should the old price be kept so you can see what it was before?
A: Yes, prices change all the time, especially sugar, rice and oil. I need to change the price of an item.
Q: Do some things have more than one price, for example one price for a single piece and another for a full carton, or different sizes of the same thing?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: When you look up a price, will you type the full name exactly, or do you want to type part of the name (like "milo") and see everything that matches?
A: No preference: you decide.

Where the client has no preference or did not answer, choose the simplest option and add nothing they did not ask for (no logins, PINs or extra required fields).
summary:
I've built your price list program in a single file, `app.py`, and all 5 of my automated checks pass. Your price list is saved in a file called `shop.db` in the same folder, so it stays there when you close the program.

What you can do with it:
- **Add an item:** give its name and price, for example `{"name": "Sugar", "price": 25.5}`. The program gives each item a number, and you use that number to look up, change or remove the item. Web address: `POST /items`
- **See everything you sell:** shows all items with their prices, in A–Z order. Web address: `GET /items`
- **Look up one item's price:** use the item's number. Web address: `GET /items/{number}`
- **Change a price:** for example when sugar, rice or oil goes up, send the new price as `{"price": 30}`. Web address: `PATCH /items/{number}`
- **Take an item off the list:** for when you stop selling it. Web address: `DELETE /items/{number}`

What the program refuses:
- An item with an empty name or no price.
- A price below zero.
- A second item with the same name as one already on the list. Capitals don't matter, so "Tea" and "tea" count as the same.
- Any item number that doesn't exist.

Where you had no preference, I chose the simplest option:
- **One price per item.** If you sell something by the piece and by the carton, add it twice with different names, like "Milo sachet" and "Milo carton".
- **Look up by item number.** To find a number, open the full list. You can't type part of a name like "milo" to search.
- **No old prices kept.** When you change a price, the old one is replaced, so you can't see what an item cost before.
